clue.text: Ménages à trois seem to her at odds with society

indicators.note: things at odds are out of agreement, so these letters fall out of their given order

parts.note: taken as written
S is the standard abbreviation for society

explanation.surface: A woman finds households of three at odds with polite society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with society' looks like part of the moral comment, but it just adds S to the letters to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A ménage à trois is a household or relationship of three lovers, which English calls a threesome.

clue.text: Novel name used occasionally with Handel's last Messiah

parts.note: Emma is Jane Austen's novel
N is the abbreviation for name

indicators.note: something done only occasionally happens every other time, so only every second letter is kept

parts.note: first and third letters of the word

indicators.note: the last of something is its final element, so only the closing letter is wanted

parts.note: final letter of the composer's name

explanation.surface: A novelty name is said to be used now and then alongside the end of Handel's oratorio Messiah.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like an anagram signal for 'name', but it is a specific novel, Austen's EMMA. Handel's Messiah is mentioned to lure you towards music.
explanation.definitionFit: Emmanuel, meaning 'God with us', is a biblical title applied to the promised Messiah in Isaiah and Matthew.

clue.text: Washington agency to go into declaration

indicators.note: going into something means ending up inside it, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: a statement is a declaration
to depart is to go

explanation.surface: A Washington agency is about to issue a formal declaration.
explanation.walkthrough: The insertion splits the declaration word after its first five letters, which then form the first word of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The State Department is the United States federal body handling foreign affairs, headquartered in Washington.

clue.text: Kitty has delightful day

parts.note: fun, used as an adjective, means enjoyable
D is the abbreviation for day

explanation.surface: A cat has a lovely day.
explanation.walkthrough: Kitty looks like a pet cat, but it is the pool of shared money.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitty is a pot of money collected for shared spending, which is a small common fund.

clue.text: Joy surrounds a funny person — circus performer?

indicators.note: to surround something is to enclose it on all sides, so one piece goes around another

parts.note: cheer is gladness or joy
taken as written
a very amusing person is said to be a riot

explanation.surface: Delight greets a comic, perhaps a clown in the big top.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the circus is the Roman Circus Maximus, where chariot races were held, not a big top with clowns.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient Roman circuses were arenas for chariot racing, so a chariot driver performed there.

clue.text: Pub dinner feels wrong without whiskey for Aussie native

indicators.note: something gone wrong is out of order, so these letters are rearranged
in its old sense 'without' means 'outside', so this letter is set alongside the others

parts.note: taken as written
Whiskey is W in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A pub meal feels off when there is no whiskey, says an Australian local.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' reads as 'lacking', which would remove a letter; here it means 'outside', so W is added to the letters before rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: The funnel-web spider is a highly venomous arachnid found only in Australia, so it is an Australian native.

clue.text: Hearts put into joint work making music

indicators.note: putting something into another thing places it inside, so one piece sits within the rest

parts.note: the hip is a joint of the body
OP is short for opus, a musical work
H is the abbreviation for hearts in card games

explanation.surface: Musicians pour their hearts into a combined project.
explanation.walkthrough: The H goes between the joint and the work, which have been set side by side. 'joint' tempts as a reference to cannabis.
explanation.definitionFit: Hip-hop is a genre of popular music built around rapping over rhythmic beats.

clue.text: Extra cash, not British, becomes burden

indicators.note: saying 'not' something excludes it, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: a bonus is extra money paid on top of wages
B is the abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: Extra money not counted as British turns into a burden.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the opening B from the extra payment leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An onus is a duty or responsibility that weighs on someone, which is a burden in the figurative sense.

clue.text: Blunt statement in house encountered with sorrow

parts.note: HO is the abbreviation for house
to have met someone is to have encountered them
ruth is an old word for pity or sorrow

explanation.surface: Harsh words spoken in a household are met with sadness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'house' looks like HOME, which is tempting given the answer, but only HO is used. Ruth, meaning sorrow, survives in 'ruthless'.
explanation.definitionFit: A home truth is an unwelcome fact about oneself, told frankly, so it is a blunt remark.

clue.text: Something nasty afoot sees leader deserting alliance

indicators.note: when the one at the front walks away, the group loses its opening member

parts.note: a bunion is a painful swelling on the foot

explanation.surface: A sinister plot is under way as the head of a coalition walks out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'afoot' suggests a scheme in progress, but it literally means on the foot, where bunions grow.
explanation.definitionFit: A union is a joining together of parties for common purpose, so it is an alliance.

clue.text: Former lover two boys lavishly praised

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
AL and TED, two short male names

explanation.surface: An ex-partner showered two young men with compliments.
explanation.walkthrough: Crosswords often use short first names such as AL and TED for 'boy' or 'man'.
explanation.definitionFit: To exalt is to glorify or extol, so someone exalted has been praised to the skies.

clue.text: Managed game in large part and cattle farms

indicators.note: having most but not all of something means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it
chess is a board game

explanation.surface: Someone oversaw hunting and also livestock estates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Managed game' reads like gamekeeping, but the game is a board game, minus its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranch is a large farm, especially in the Americas, where cattle are raised.

clue.text: Complete report

definitions.meaning: first meaning: whole and in good condition
second meaning: a noise, as the report of a gun

explanation.walkthrough: A report here is a bang, like a gunshot, not a written document.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means whole and undamaged, and the noun is anything heard, such as the bang of a firearm.

clue.text: Point about much reduced page is so long

indicators.note: to be about something is to go round it, so one piece wraps the rest

parts.note: the tip of something is its point

indicators.note: something reduced has been cut down, so a letter is trimmed off the end

parts.note: oodles is an informal word for a great deal
P is the abbreviation for page

explanation.surface: Making a point about a heavily cut page can take a long time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so long' looks like a measure of length but is a farewell. Toodle-pip is a jaunty, dated British goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: Both expressions are informal ways of saying goodbye, so the British farewell is a synonym.

clue.text: Deter a tour abroad that caravans might have taken

indicators.note: abroad can mean widely scattered or astray, so these letters wander out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone discourages a foreign trip that people with holiday trailers might have made.
explanation.walkthrough: The caravans are desert trains of camels and merchants, not holiday trailers, which is what makes the definition fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Merchants travelling in caravans followed established paths for commerce, such as the Silk Road.

clue.text: Stuffing not put back in bear

parts.note: padding is soft stuffing material

indicators.note: putting something back returns it the way it came, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The filling of a teddy is not pushed back inside it.
explanation.walkthrough: Stuffing and bear together suggest a teddy, which is apt since the answer is a famous toy bear.
explanation.definitionFit: Paddington is the marmalade-loving bear of Michael Bond's children's books, named after a London railway station.

clue.text: Disguised in Emerald Isle, a spy: Tees won't blab

indicators.note: something disguised has had its appearance altered, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An undercover agent in Ireland promises the setter will keep quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: Tees is this puzzle's setter, so the definition is the setter saying 'I won't tell'. The Emerald Isle is Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a promise to keep a secret, which is what someone refusing to blab would say.

clue.text: Such women could be out in north, beset by male prejudice

parts.note: Les is a man's name

indicators.note: to be beset is to be surrounded on all sides, so one piece is hemmed in

parts.note: bias is prejudice
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: Women who are openly gay in the north of England face male prejudice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'male' reads as an adjective with 'prejudice', but it gives a man's name. 'could be' marks the definition as one example, not a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: To be out is to have openly declared one's sexuality, so gay women may be described that way.

clue.text: Royals partying are changing the whole calendar

indicators.note: people partying are moving about wildly, so these letters are scattered
changing means altering form, so these letters take a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Members of the royal family at a party are rearranging their entire diary.
explanation.walkthrough: Two anagram signals cover the two parts of the fodder, which are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: The calendar runs through one full cycle of the Earth round the Sun, so a complete calendar spans that period.

clue.text: Haze affected toil in smoggy city

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece is placed within another

parts.note: Los Angeles, famous for its smog

indicators.note: something affected has been acted on and altered, so these letters change order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Pollution hampered work in a smoggy city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Haze' looks like smog, matching the surface, but it is a surname: Dolores Haze is the title character of Nabokov's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: In Nabokov's novel, Lolita is the nickname of the girl whose full name is Dolores Haze.

clue.text: South American greeting tasty Asian dish

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for south
US for the United States, hence American
hi is a greeting

explanation.surface: A South American says hello over a delicious Asian meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South American' reads as one phrase about the continent but splits into two separate abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is the Japanese dish of vinegared rice with raw fish or other toppings.

clue.text: Jazz group touring see capital city

indicators.note: to tour is to travel all the way round, so one piece circles another

parts.note: a combo is a small jazz band
lo is an old word meaning look or see

explanation.surface: A jazz band on tour goes to see a capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' sounds like an instruction to visit, but it is the archaic interjection, as in 'lo and behold'.
explanation.definitionFit: Colombo is the commercial capital and former official capital of Sri Lanka.

clue.text: Youngster close to stone block

parts.note: a cub is a young animal, or a junior Scout

indicators.note: the close of something is its end, so only the final letter is used

parts.note: final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A child stands next to a stone slab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close to' looks like a phrase of position, but it picks the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A cube is a solid with six equal square faces, like a building block or a block of ice.

clue.text: Enduring a considerable noise inside

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: being inside means lying within, so one piece is enclosed by another

parts.note: big means large or considerable
a din is a loud noise

explanation.surface: Putting up with a great racket indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Enduring' tempts as meaning tolerating the noise, but it is the definition in the sense of long-lasting.
explanation.definitionFit: Something abiding persists over time and does not fade, so it is lasting or durable.

clue.text: Woodsman thus given the push?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a woodcutter is equipped with a chopping tool
second meaning: dismissed from a job

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is a playful coinage meaning 'carrying an axe'; the question mark admits it. 'Given the push' is informal British for sacked.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sacked is called being axed, and a woodcutter with his tool could jokingly be said to be so too.

clue.text: Don't declare weapon

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in cricket, keep batting rather than close the innings
second meaning: a police officer's truncheon

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a captain declares to end the team's innings early; choosing not to means carrying on batting, read here as two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket side that carries on batting rather than declaring will 'bat on', and a baton is a club used as a weapon.

clue.text: Hot tureen needs stir in addition to that

indicators.note: stirring something mixes it about, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A hot soup bowl needs a stir as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stir' looks like an instruction for the soup, which neatly fits a tureen.
explanation.definitionFit: Thereunto is a formal, old-fashioned word meaning besides or moreover, added to what came before.
